summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and morbid obesity was admitted for severe abdominal pain and hyperglycemia, found to be in hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state. She had recently run out of insulin pen needles, contributing to poor glycemic control. Workup revealed a right great toe infection with purulent drainage; after toenail avulsion and persistent leukocytosis, MRI confirmed osteomyelitis, leading to right hallux amputation. She was treated with IV Zosyn, later transitioned to oral Augmentin. Abdominal pain was attributed to gastroparesis, with no acute surgical cause found. She received a blood transfusion for worsening microcytic anemia and was managed for pseudohyponatremia, which resolved with glucose control. She was discharged home on Augmentin, increased insulin doses, and pain control, with follow-up for foot healing, anemia, and outpatient mammography for incidental breast calcifications.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperosmolarity without nonketotic hyperglycemic-hyperosmolar coma (NKHHC)
Anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
